dateline: Bamako / Kidal / Ménaka / Kompienbiga / Barsalogho / Titao / Goubré — 2012–Present
heroHeadline: Bamako Siege Day 34: Post-Eid Holds; IRC: 5.1M Malians Need Aid; Goïta Reshuffles Theater Commands
heroSubtitle: Day 34 of JNIM's declared 'total siege' of Bamako (announced April 28, 2026). The March 2026 fuel truce has formally expired; JNIM retains structural road-junction control to reinstate any level of blockade at will with no diplomatic framework in place. The International Rescue Committee's one-month assessment (published June 1) documents 5.1 million Malians in need of humanitarian assistance, 1.5 million at crisis-level hunger, and 1M+ children facing severe acute malnutrition — while WFP requires $453M for the next 6 months on top of its existing $620M funding gap that already suspended operations for 2M people. The US Embassy's Enhanced Security Alert expired May 31 with no announced renewal. Three of six supply corridors remain cut (Amnesty International, May 15); food prices +43–65% above pre-siege baselines. FAO projects 52.8M at IPC Phase 3+ during the June–August lean season. On May 29–30, Goïta announced a military theater command restructure appointing Colonel-Major Karim Traoré, Colonel-Major Didier Dembélé, and Colonel Issa Bagayoko to geographic theater commands, with General Makan Alassane Diarra heading AES Unified Force coordination — a reshuffle framed as a response to the command failures of April 25–May 13 that cost Defence Minister Camara's life, the loss of Kidal, and JNIM's 9-hour occupation of Djibo. Three key fronts remain active: (1) BAMAKO BLOCKADE (Day 34): Post-Eid window (May 28–June 5) ongoing with no new major JNIM escalation confirmed — but JNIM's structural control of supply-junction access roads unchanged. WFP suspended; IRC emergency response active. (2) KIDAL AERIAL CAMPAIGN: FAMa/Africa Corps continue striking FLA/JNIM-held Kidal with Su-type fighters and armed drones; city remains under FLA control. (3) BURKINA FASO: Five major JNIM atrocities in May 2026 killed approximately 300+ (Bagare VDP post May 1–2, Djibo occupation May 11, Diapaga seizure May 13, Goubré IDP camp May 22, Kompienbiga market May 31) plus the Barsalogho ICRC convoy attack (May 29–30, 13 killed including ICRC personnel — a grave IHL breach). The Traoré junta remains under pressure after closing Ouagadougou's Grand Mosque and detaining ~100 protesters on May 29 following the arrest of Islamic scholar Imam Mohamed Kindo.
